title: Cities: Skylines | Franklin, Episode 3: Founding Franklin
premise: Donoteat argues that Franklin’s rational green-country-town plan is immediately reshaped by port commerce, property subdivision and exploitative colonial labor, with distilling embedded in that economy.
coverage: The classroom slide sequence leads into Franklin’s street grid, port growth, coerced labor and whiskey economy, ending with a tour of the town. Historical claims are the presenter’s account; the city and founder are fictional. Projector-like sounds accompany slide changes, though their exact mechanical source is uncertain.

panels.heading: Opening identity
panels.description: Orange FRANKLIN and white A DONOTEAT SERIES lettering over the completed colonial town.
panels.camera: The opening cuts between black, the title and several aerial views of the town.
panels.action: Title lettering appears over city images.

panels.heading: Episode 3: Founding Franklin
panels.description: Episode title at upper left over the wide regional game map.
panels.camera: Wide overhead map; subsequent views move closer to the river settlements.
panels.action: Map navigation begins.

panels.heading: Fight me: setup
panels.description: Road-tool gameplay over forest and river accompanies the invitation to fight over planning politics.
panels.camera: The overhead gameplay reframes around the road work.
panels.action: Blue road previews and a red invalid placement line change.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the Uwe Boll reversal: the confident fight invitation is about to be contradicted by the follow notification and boxing insert.

panels.heading: A dangerous new follower
panels.description: White notification reads Uwe Boll and Mark Morris followed you · 2h.
panels.camera: Static notification composited over overhead gameplay.
panels.action: Notification appears; underlying road placement continues.
panels.visualGag: Uwe Boll’s name in the follow notification turns the fight invitation into a threat, followed by the boxing footage.

panels.heading: Boxing payoff
panels.description: Live-action boxing ring: black-clad boxer, red-clad opponent and white-shirted referee.
panels.camera: Hard cut from gameplay to boxing footage, with changing ring positions and shot compositions.
panels.action: The boxers and referee change position in the ring.
panels.visualGag: Inserted fight footage makes the Lowtax/Uwe Boll reference concrete and punctures the challenge; connected to the concession after the cut back.

panels.heading: I concede
panels.description: Back to top-down game road construction beside a river.
panels.camera: Hard cut back to the overhead game view.
panels.action: Road preview changes angle and terrain tools follow.
panels.visualGag: After the fight invitation, follow notification and boxing footage, the narrator concedes to Boll.

panels.heading: Microphone thanks
panels.description: White B SQUICKLE lettering at bottom over terrain editing.
panels.camera: The overhead terrain view changes scale and position.
panels.action: Colored circular terrain brush moves over the landscape.

panels.heading: Dutch conquest
panels.description: Red-white-blue horizontal Dutch tricolor overlays game terrain.
panels.camera: Static Dutch flag over game terrain, followed by the Union flag.
panels.action: Flag appears during the Dutch conquest summary.
panels.notes: The Dutch flag appears after the conquest phrase begins, then gives way to the Union flag.

panels.heading: British conquest follows
panels.description: Union flag replaces the Dutch tricolor over game terrain.
panels.camera: Static Union flag over terrain.
panels.action: Flag replacement summarizes successive conquest without staged warfare.
panels.notes: The flag change summarizes conquest without reenacting a battle.

panels.heading: Other Paradox games
panels.description: Europa Universalis IV strategy-game screenshot, with a map centered on TEXAS, is inset over Cities: Skylines.
panels.camera: Static screenshot overlay; no battle action visible.
panels.action: Inset appears, then disappears.
panels.visualGag: The demand for conquest footage gets a screenshot of Paradox’s Europa Universalis IV instead of warfare in Franklin. Its incongruous Texas empire adds to the aside.

panels.heading: Urban planning is art
panels.description: Regional game map with a two-lane-road tooltip.
panels.camera: The wide overhead map gives way to closer views of the road layout.
panels.action: Road tool remains open.

panels.heading: Architecture versus engineering
panels.description: Photograph of a house stranded between lanes of a newly built road.
panels.camera: Static centered photo insert over gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character movement in the photograph.
panels.visualGag: The house stranded between road lanes counters the reduction of planning to traffic engineering. Its location and backstory are unknown.

panels.heading: Lecture apparatus: setup
panels.description: Terrain contours and road preview before the projector photograph.
panels.camera: Overhead game view.
panels.action: Road construction continues.
panels.visualGag: Connected projector/classroom gag setup: architectural expertise supposedly requires a Kodak Carousel, followed by the literal projector and faux projected slides.

panels.heading: A Kodak Carousel is required
panels.description: Centered photograph of a gray carousel slide projector over the game.
panels.camera: Static product-photo insert.
panels.action: Projector image appears; no operator is shown.
panels.visualGag: The Kodak Carousel photograph turns architectural expertise into classroom equipment. After the grad-student line and a pause, projector-like noise begins the simulated lecture.

panels.heading: Urban Planning 101
panels.description: Rounded, vignetted slide reads URBAN PLANNING 101 / from prehistory to the 17th century over a city map.
panels.camera: The slide emerges from black and blur, comes into focus, then holds.
panels.action: The slide sharpens and holds.

sound.text: Projector-like setup noise accompanies the slide coming into focus.

panels.visualGag: Audiovisual payoff to projector-photo/grad-student setup: after the pause, projector-like noise accompanies the blurred slide coming into focus, turning the game into an old-fashioned lecture. Subsequent slide advances repeat the gag.

panels.heading: Gilgamesh, via Star Trek
panels.description: Star Trek: The Next Generation still shows Jean-Luc Picard beside the ridged-forehead Tamarian captain Dathon outdoors, rather than an archaeological city image.
panels.camera: The image replaces black, appears blurred, then sharpens into a fixed slide.
panels.action: Picard and Dathon remain in a static television still.

sound.text: A projector-like burst accompanies the slide change and refocusing.

panels.visualGag: Picard and Dathon from Star Trek: The Next Generation illustrate Gilgamesh in a likely Darmok reference. A mechanical burst and the refocusing slide repeat the classroom-projector gag.

panels.heading: A plan we can look at
panels.description: Old map labeled LE PIRÉE, with harbor outlines and street pattern.
panels.camera: A black-and-blurred transition resolves into the static map.
panels.action: Map replaces television still.

sound.text: Another projector-like burst accompanies the map slide’s arrival.

panels.visualGag: The next-slide request gets another mechanical burst, followed by the map coming into focus.

panels.heading: The dirtiest word: grid
panels.description: Overhead image of regular street blocks and a green square.
panels.camera: Black gives way to a blurred street-grid slide that sharpens and holds.
panels.action: Street-grid image replaces Piraeus map.

sound.text: Projector-like slide-change noise accompanies the grid reveal.

panels.visualGag: The dirtiest-word tease reveals an ordinary grid. A slide request, mechanical noise and simulated refocusing repeat the projector joke.

panels.heading: Etruscan visual detour
panels.description: A game-rendered boar sculpture in a fenced, fern-filled garden surrounded by benches.
panels.camera: A black transition gives way to the fixed, rounded slide.
panels.action: Static game asset image.

sound.text: A projector-like burst accompanies the boar-park slide.
Another projector-like burst precedes the Roman fort plan.

panels.visualGag: The Etruscan discussion gets an unexpected boar-park illustration whose exact reference is unclear. Mechanical bursts accompany this slide and the Roman fort plan that follows.

panels.heading: Roman castrum
panels.description: Black-and-white fort plan divided into regular blocks.
panels.camera: The blurred replacement sharpens into a static fort plan.
panels.action: Diagram appears.
panels.visualGag: The Roman fort plan appears through black, blur and refocusing after the preceding projector-like sound.

panels.heading: Cardo and decumanus
panels.description: Fort diagram gains red vertical CARDO and green horizontal DECUMONUS labels.
panels.camera: The slide passes through black and blur before the labelled plan comes into focus.
panels.action: Colored axes annotate the plan.

sound.text: A projector-like burst accompanies the street-axis slide.

panels.visualGag: The next-slide request adds the street axes with another mechanical burst and simulated refocusing.

panels.heading: Forum means forum
panels.description: Simtropolis website screenshot with the Forums section visible.
panels.camera: The website replaces black and blur, then holds in focus.
panels.action: Static website screenshot replaces ancient plan.
panels.visualGag: Wordplay: Roman civic forum becomes an internet city-building forum; connected to the preceding axes and narrated intersection.

panels.heading: A distorted surviving grid
panels.description: Aerial photograph of Florence with dense reddish rooftops and partially regular streets.
panels.camera: The aerial photograph appears through black and blur, then holds in focus.
panels.action: Photograph appears.

panels.heading: Medieval urban problems
panels.description: Engraved riverside view labeled LONDON.
panels.camera: The replacement sharpens into a fixed engraving.
panels.action: Static engraving.

panels.heading: Renaissance ideal city
panels.description: Perspective painting of an orderly plaza with central fountain and classical buildings.
panels.camera: The painting comes into focus after a black-and-blurred slide change.
panels.action: The painting holds.

sound.text: A projector-like burst accompanies the ideal-city slide.

panels.visualGag: Another next-slide request gets a mechanical burst and the ideal-city painting coming into focus.

panels.heading: Order at building scale
panels.description: Photograph of arcaded hospital facade and square.
panels.camera: The architectural photograph emerges from black and blur, then sharpens.
panels.action: Static architectural photograph.

sound.text: A projector-like burst accompanies the hospital-facade slide.

panels.visualGag: The projector noise and simulated refocusing replace the ideal-city painting with an example of order at building scale.

panels.heading: Facade, not wholesale reconstruction
panels.description: Photograph of a church with finished lower facade and rough upper masonry.
panels.camera: The photograph replaces black, comes into focus and holds.
panels.action: Static architecture image.

panels.heading: Baroque Rome
panels.description: Two domed churches on a plaza, with pedestrians in the photograph.
panels.camera: The blurred Baroque slide comes into focus and holds.
panels.action: The pedestrians remain still in the photograph.

sound.text: A brief projector-like burst accompanies the Baroque slide.

panels.visualGag: A brief projector-like noise precedes the Baroque image coming into focus.

panels.heading: Our founder?
panels.description: Portrait-like still of Danny DeVito as Frank Reynolds from It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, wearing a brown vest and colonial-costume clothing.
panels.camera: The portrait appears after black and holds.
panels.action: Static character still.
panels.visualGag: Danny DeVito’s Frank Reynolds from It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia stands in for William Franklin. A Frank/Franklin pun may be intended; the exact television episode is uncertain. Episode 4 widens the same image to include Charlie Day.

panels.heading: Franklin by crossing out Philadelphia
panels.description: Antique Philadelphia plan has its city name struck through in red and FRANKLIN written beside it.
panels.camera: The static map overlays the resumed gameplay, then clears.
panels.action: Edited name relabels the historic plan.
panels.visualGag: Transparent fictional renaming is the joke: Philadelphia remains legible under the red strike-through while the plan is presented as Franklin.

panels.heading: Center-square precedents
panels.description: Modern aerial photograph of a town center square over the game.
panels.camera: A static aerial inset gives way to a second view of a center square.
panels.action: Illustrative inset changes; game continues beneath.

panels.heading: Inherited street names
panels.description: Large MARKET STREET / BROAD STREET / MAIN STREET / HIGH STREET list over game.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay, static white text.
panels.action: Road-building previews change beneath the list.

panels.heading: Four common squares
panels.description: Renamed antique plan returns with four bright-green squares.
panels.camera: Static annotated map overlay.
panels.action: Four squares are highlighted.
panels.visualGag: The crossed-out Philadelphia map returns as Franklin, now with green annotations marking four squares.

panels.heading: Greene Country Towne
panels.description: Large white GREENE COUNTRY TOWNE caption over sparse game blocks.
panels.camera: Overhead game view; scale changes in surrounding views.
panels.action: Caption appears as roads are laid.
panels.visualGag: Mock-archaic spelling packages the utopian green-town slogan; connected to the final grim welcome reversal.

panels.heading: Low-density lots and tolerance
panels.description: Large mostly wooded rectangular blocks outlined by dirt roads.
panels.camera: Overhead views change between the individual blocks and the whole town.
panels.action: Building placement begins within large parcels.
panels.visualGag: Visual setup for green-town reversal: the spacious grid will later be occupied unevenly by port density.

panels.heading: The port fixes the economics
panels.description: Timber dock buildings and road approach beside the river.
panels.camera: A closer overhead view of the dock follows the wider town views.
panels.action: Dock/road tools and horse vehicle options are manipulated.

panels.heading: Subdividing the ideal
panels.description: Long red-brick building and open lots near the waterfront.
panels.camera: The overhead view moves closer to the waterfront streets.
panels.action: Buildings are placed and new road/lot previews appear.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to spacious-lot setup: port development begins filling and subdividing the ideal town.

panels.heading: Rich houses, small houses, immigrants
panels.description: Growing waterfront blocks, including large red-brick houses and small neighboring structures.
panels.camera: Changing overhead views show the growing waterfront neighborhood.
panels.action: Construction placement previews continue.

panels.heading: Three passage mechanisms
panels.description: PENAL TRANSPORTATION and INDENTURED SERVITUDE appear over building gameplay, followed by ATLANTIC SLAVE TRADE.
panels.camera: Overhead game plus static list.
panels.action: The list builds from one line to three.

panels.heading: Indenture: setup for a modern analogy
panels.description: INDENTURED SERVITUDE appears over gameplay after the three-line passage list is complete.
panels.camera: Static heading over overhead streets.
panels.action: Building tool remains active.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the Musk/rocket/Mars inserts that translate the wealthy sponsor and colonial passage into a modern space-colonization analogy.

panels.heading: The wealthy sponsor
panels.description: Elon Musk photograph before a SPACEX logo.
panels.camera: Static photo overlay.
panels.action: No visible photographed movement.
panels.visualGag: First payoff in the indenture analogy: a modern billionaire substitutes visually for the wealthy person in the contract.

panels.heading: Transportation to the colony
panels.description: SpaceX rocket-launch photograph.
panels.camera: The Musk photograph gives way to a static rocket-launch image.
panels.action: Rocket is visibly launching in a still photograph.
panels.visualGag: Connected indenture/Musk/Mars gag: transportation becomes a space launch.

panels.heading: New-world destination
panels.description: Large orange-red image of Mars over colonial-town gameplay.
panels.camera: Static planet image replaces launch photograph.
panels.action: The Mars image holds over the gameplay.
panels.visualGag: Connected analogy relocates the colonial destination to Mars.

panels.heading: Labor on Mars
panels.description: Illustration of an astronaut working outside a small Mars settlement.
panels.camera: Static illustration replaces planet image.
panels.action: The illustration depicts an astronaut tending equipment.
panels.visualGag: Final payoff to the modern indenture sequence: unpaid colonial service is rendered as labor in a Mars outpost.

panels.heading: Fixed term, qualified consent
panels.description: Back to developing Franklin blocks with blue building previews.
panels.camera: Hard cut back to overhead gameplay, followed by changing neighborhood views.
panels.action: Row-house placement continues.

panels.heading: Parents control childrens contracts
panels.description: Dense rows of houses and vacant gridded plots, with placement menus.
panels.camera: Overhead neighborhood view.
panels.action: Building previews fill small lots.

panels.heading: Apprentice in quotation marks
panels.description: White “APPRENTICE” caption over town construction.
panels.camera: Fixed text over overhead game.
panels.action: Caption appears.
panels.visualGag: Scare quotes undermine the nominal promise of education before narration describes field and mine labor.

panels.heading: Human cash on delivery
panels.description: Waterfront town and rows of newly placed buildings.
panels.camera: Town-wide views give way to closer rows of houses.
panels.action: Buildings are selected and moved; no literal market is represented by the game.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the later £5 redemptioner-price caption and contrasting £200 chattel-slavery caption. This is an explanatory price comparison, not a comic claim that the labor systems are equivalent.

panels.heading: Redemptioner price: five pounds
panels.description: Huge white £5 caption over rows of houses and game placement tools.
panels.camera: Static £5 text over gameplay.
panels.action: Price caption appears during the five-British-pounds explanation.
panels.visualGag: Visual price-comparison setup for the later £200 caption: fixed-term indenture is priced differently from hereditary lifetime ownership. Explanatory contrast, not treated as an amusing auction or equivalence.
panels.notes: The £5 caption compares fixed-term indenture with hereditary lifetime enslavement; it is not an equivalence.

panels.heading: Penal transportation
panels.description: PENAL TRANSPORTATION heading over city blocks.
panels.camera: Overhead view with static title.
panels.action: Heading appears and disappears as construction continues.

panels.heading: Terms and transported Irish prisoners
panels.description: Row houses and a highlighted red-brick block in game.
panels.camera: Overhead reframing between neighborhoods.
panels.action: Building placement/selection continues; no prisoner transport is visually enacted.

panels.heading: Misleading labels: setup
panels.description: Large quoted “IRISH SLAVERY” caption over town.
panels.camera: Static text over overhead game.
panels.action: Label appears in quotation marks.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the later InfoWars quarantine: the captions display terms the narrator explicitly rejects, not endorsements of those labels.

panels.heading: White slavery label challenged
panels.description: Quoted “WHITE SLAVERY” replaces the earlier label.
panels.camera: Text replacement over changing overhead streets.
panels.action: Label appears then vanishes.
panels.visualGag: Connected rejected-label/InfoWars sequence: the misleading term is introduced for rebuttal and later visually quarantined.

panels.heading: Chattel slavery is different
panels.description: CHATTEL SLAVERY caption over building gameplay.
panels.camera: Static heading over overhead game; scale and location change around it.
panels.action: Heading appears.

panels.heading: Roman comparison insert
panels.description: Recognizable Ben-Hur Roman-galley still shows a helmeted officer in a red cloak among crowded rowing benches.
panels.camera: Static cinematic inset over game.
panels.action: The still shows seated rowers and a standing officer.
panels.visualGag: The Ben-Hur galley illustrates the narrator’s hyperbolic lifetime-spa comparison. Above it, the game ticker reads “Rap Music Causes Hangnails, Study Shows”; whether the timing is deliberate is unclear.

panels.heading: The slave ship
panels.description: Historical diagram packs human figures into two ship-deck plans.
panels.camera: The static ship diagram overlays gameplay, then clears.
panels.action: No character animation; figures are diagrammatic.

panels.heading: Two hundred pounds, many lifetimes
panels.description: Huge £200 caption overlays the city.
panels.camera: Fixed price caption over overhead gameplay.
panels.action: Price appears then disappears.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the earlier £5 redemptioner-price visual: £200 reinforces the narrated contrast with permanent, hereditary ownership. This is a grave explanatory comparison, not an equivalence or joke about enslavement.

panels.heading: Permanent legal dispossession
panels.description: White list: PROPERTY FOR LIFE / NO LEGAL RIGHTS / NO MEANS OF LEGAL RECOURSE / NEARLY LIVESTOCK.
panels.camera: The list builds over gameplay until all four lines are visible.
panels.action: The list accumulates over the city.

panels.heading: Nowhere to escape
panels.description: Town blocks with row houses, mills, empty plots and placement tools.
panels.camera: Changing overhead game framing.
panels.action: Construction continues; no escape sequence is depicted.

panels.heading: The modern misuse of history
panels.description: Wider riverfront grid and buildings as the narrator discusses modern slavery apologetics.
panels.camera: The wide riverfront view gives way to nearer blocks.
panels.action: Buildings are added and selected.
panels.visualGag: The presenter’s attack on modern slavery apologetics sets up the InfoWars quarantine gag.

panels.heading: Quarantine at InfoWars
panels.description: Large black-and-white INFOWARS.COM logo with “WHITE SLAVERY” text across it.
panels.camera: The logo overlays the wide town view before gameplay resumes.
panels.action: Logo/text overlay appears.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the rejected Irish/white-slavery labels: the phrase is visibly sent to InfoWars rather than retained as an explanatory category.

panels.heading: Cheap and exploitable labor
panels.description: Increasingly dense town blocks and remaining large empty squares.
panels.camera: Overhead town view alternates scale in successive views.
panels.action: Construction fills houses and service buildings.

panels.heading: No wages needed
panels.description: Town-wide and street-level overhead views show dense waterfront housing beside open interior plots.
panels.camera: The overhead view alternates between the whole town and closer housing rows.
panels.action: Town decoration and placement continue.

panels.heading: Masters and colonial industry
panels.description: Densely built dirt-street blocks with a terrain/detail brush.
panels.camera: The overhead view shifts rapidly among neighborhood compositions.
panels.action: Surface/detail brush moves along streets and buildings.

panels.heading: Distilling and the western farms
panels.description: Church with a cemetery filled by repeated gravestone props.
panels.camera: The overhead view closes in on the cemetery.
panels.action: Gravestone props are placed and selected.

panels.heading: Rain, corn, whiskey
panels.description: Overhead neighborhood view with row houses, dirt streets and placement tools during the corn/whiskey lyric.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay before the singer photograph.
panels.action: Detail placement continues; the singer photograph appears in the next panel briefly.
panels.visualGag: The rain/corn/whiskey lyric sets up a singer photograph on “frisky”. The possible Luke Bryan reference remains uncertain.

panels.heading: Frisky: brief singer-photo payoff
panels.description: Smiling man in dark cap and plaid shirt, in-ear monitor and hand on a microphone/stand, under purple stage lighting; photograph overlays Front Street gameplay and barrel props.
panels.camera: A brief static singer photograph overlays gameplay.
panels.action: The photograph appears briefly, then clears.
panels.visualGag: The singer photograph lands on “frisky” in the rain/corn/whiskey lyric. The man may be Luke Bryan, and the lyric matches “Rain Is a Good Thing.”
panels.notes: The singer’s identity is uncertain; the lyric matches “Rain Is a Good Thing.”

panels.heading: Back to whiskey transport economics
panels.description: Overhead wooden docks and barrels beside the waterfront after the brief singer photograph disappears.
panels.camera: Return to overhead waterfront gameplay.
panels.action: Detail placement continues beneath the corn/whiskey transport explanation.
panels.visualGag: The singer photograph clears, ending the pop-culture detour as the narration returns to colonial transport costs.
panels.notes: The narration returns to transport costs.

panels.heading: Turning bulky grain into value
panels.description: House and surrounding row houses, open yard, trees and dirt streets during the grain-to-whiskey explanation.
panels.camera: Overhead neighborhood gameplay before the book cover.
panels.action: Ground/prop details are edited.

panels.heading: The Alcoholic Republic: source shown
panels.description: Red book cover reads THE ALCOHOLIC REPUBLIC / AN AMERICAN TRADITION / W. J. RORABAUGH over neighborhood gameplay.
panels.camera: Static book cover over gameplay.
panels.action: Book cover appears as the presenter cites it, then is gone by the early bushel caption.
panels.notes: The cited author is W. J. Rorabaugh.

panels.heading: A bushel becomes whiskey
panels.description: The churchyard calculation begins with 1 BUSHEL (~9 GALLONS) CORN @25 CENTS, then adds =2.5 GALLONS WHISKEY WORTH $1.25.
panels.camera: Static calculation grows from one line into two.
panels.action: Calculation text accumulates.

panels.heading: Whiskey as currency
panels.description: White 1. WHISKEY WAS AN INFORMAL MODE OF EXCHANGE over a wide view of the grid.
panels.camera: Wide overhead town with centered text.
panels.action: First numbered reason appears.

panels.heading: Habitually drunk
panels.description: White 2. MOST COLONISTS ARE HABITUALLY DRUNK over the city; later farm plots are painted.
panels.camera: Wide overhead view, then closer field views.
panels.action: Second reason replaces first; fields are added.
panels.visualGag: Deadpan second-item payoff to the sober economic first reason: the reason list ends in habitual drunkenness.

panels.heading: Liquor wages and the green-town callback
panels.description: Open farm blocks and small houses beside dense rows.
panels.camera: Overhead views change scale around the farm blocks.
panels.action: Field colors/surfaces are painted.
panels.visualGag: Setup and beginning of the final welcome reversal: productive open land coexists with the inequality described in the ironic green-town welcome.

panels.heading: Welcome to Franklin: reversal
panels.description: Open dirt roads and fenced farm plots remain under construction.
panels.camera: Overhead farm-block view.
panels.action: White fences are laid along parcel boundaries.
panels.visualGag: The GREENE COUNTRY TOWNE promise ends in an ironic welcome to slavery, sewers, drunkenness, disease and crime.

panels.heading: Worse before better
panels.description: Close view of small rural building, brown yard and road, with fence selection panel.
panels.camera: A closer overhead view follows the fence placement.
panels.action: Final yard/fence detailing.
panels.visualGag: Ends the green-town reversal with the explicit next-episode promise that conditions worsen.

panels.heading: Finished town: church and cemetery
panels.description: UI-free view of white clock-tower church, rows of red-brick houses, cemetery and horses.
panels.camera: Black gives way to a cinematic church view that pulls back to include more of the cemetery.
panels.action: Horses and tiny pedestrians are visible around the church and houses.

panels.heading: Dirt streets and row houses
panels.description: UI-free low oblique view along brick row houses, muddy street puddles and horses.
panels.camera: A cut introduces a lateral fly-through along the street-facing facades.
panels.action: Horse and pedestrian positions change along the muddy street.

panels.heading: The port draws the town
panels.description: Wide low aerial view across town toward river, then down a broad dirt street toward waterfront warehouses.
panels.camera: A new view shifts across the town toward the waterfront.
panels.action: Town showcased without game UI.

panels.heading: Harbor and warehouses
panels.description: Overhead oblique view of warehouses and projecting wooden piers.
panels.camera: Cut to the waterfront, followed by a different roof-level angle.
panels.action: Waterfront shown without UI.

panels.heading: Rooftops, churchyards, and river
panels.description: High oblique view over roofs, cemetery blocks, warehouses and docks.
panels.camera: Changing elevated views show the town and port from several angles.
panels.action: Scenic town montage continues.

panels.heading: Last close city pass
panels.description: Low oblique churchyard and nearby white/brick buildings.
panels.camera: A close rooftop view gives way to the church and cemetery.
panels.action: The town showcase continues.

panels.heading: Finished density, unbuilt hinterland
panels.description: Aerial view of dense waterfront row houses, followed by increasingly wide regional views.
panels.camera: The aerial view pulls outward from the town to the whole grid and region, then darkens.
panels.action: City recedes into the regional map.
panels.visualGag: Visual callback to the green-town reversal: dense waterfront remains a small edge of an enormous mostly empty planned grid.

panels.heading: Donoteat closing mark
panels.description: Circular coin-like logo with diagonal stripe and DNE lettering on black.
panels.camera: The centered DNE logo follows the black transition.
panels.action: The logo appears on black.

panels.heading: End on black
panels.description: The screen stays black through the ending.
panels.camera: Black hold; no camera motion.
panels.action: No visible action.
